messages:
anya: Hey all — dropping the company OKR draft for FY26 Q3 into the thread. I tried to consolidate exec feedback and the customer-driven asks. Please review the scope sections (A/B/C) and the launch criteria on the right column.

anya: Link: https://drive.redwood/company/okr/fy26q3/draft — see 'Top-level tradeoffs' tab. TL;DR: we trimmed two stretch initiatives to keep Dedicated & Private launch timelines intact.

miguel: skimmed. Quick q: why are we still keeping ‘multi-region fallback’ in scope A? that’s a heavy infra lift and will push Dedicated by ~3w.

sarah: we left it because a handful of enterprise pilots require geo-residency at launch. if we drop it to B we risk losing the pilot accounts that are tied to their infra contracts.

devon: from eng perspective — making fallback work reliably needs new routing + kv-cache replication. estimate: 3 engs x 3 weeks. not trivial.

cecilia: customer ask list (from AMs): bankcorp and mediportal both listed multi-region as must-have. They signed LOIs contingent on it. We can try to negotiate a phased rollout (pilot regions first).

anya: proposal: keep multi-region in A but reduce scope: GA is single-region with automated failover (no hot-cache replicate). full cache replication moves to B. that saves ~2w of effort.

miguel: ok that trade sounds reasonable. can we reflect that in the launch criteria text? current wording is ambiguous.

anya: updated wording pasted below:

```
Launch criteria - Multi-region (revised):
- Pilot: automated DNS failover with cold-warm cache restore verified in 2 regions.
- GA: automated failover with validated SLOs; cache-replication (hot) in scope B.
- Acceptance: 2 pilot customers (bankcorp, mediportal) signed off and perf < 150ms p95 for failed-region routing.
```

sarah: love that. add: include data residency checklist completed + audit log retention confirmation.

devon: noted. will need a short spike for the DNS failover testing harness. I'll put a 5 day spike on the schedule.

kevin-ct0: higher level ask — are we confident removing the two stretch initiatives will not hurt our FY26 roadmap narrative to investors? we should keep one growth-facing stretch to show ambition.

anya: yeah — we kept 'Optimize throughput with quantized models' as a stretch (C -> A?) suggestion: move it to A as a measurable stretch (reduce gen cost by 20%). but that comes with risk to latency SLOs.

miguel: if we move quantization to A, we must guarantee fallbacks to float models on regression. that doubles rollout QA effort.

cecilia: customers love cost reductions, but they care more about reliability. prefer it stays as B-stretch.

anya: ok decision record: quantization stays in B-stretch. multi-region modified as above and remains in A. I'll update the doc and mark the scope changes.

sarah: can product execs + eng leads sign off by EOD Friday? we need this to go to finance to finalize resource allocations.

okrs-bot: Reminder: OKR signoff deadline set for 2026-04-03 17:00 UTC. Current approvals: 2/5.

miguel: +1 (approve) :thumbsup:

devon: +1 (approve) — will deliver DNS spike and testing harness.

cecilia: +1 — will negotiate phased pilot contract language with AMs.

anya: thanks — Kevin, Sarah, last two please?

kevin-ct0: reviewed, leaving conditional approval: +1 if we keep one measurable growth stretch (we'll swap in a marketing experiment if needed). otherwise fine.

sarah: +1 — approving the revised draft. will put a calendar invite for the sign-off sync tomorrow 10am PT.

anya: awesome, I'll update the doc with the exact acceptance criteria and ping legal for the pilot amendment language. leaving next actions in the doc's 'decision log' section.

anya: tagging final checklist
- [ ] update doc
- [ ] send pilot amendment draft to legal
- [ ] schedule finance handoff

sarah: noted. :eyes:

anya: thanks everyone, will post the updated draft shortly. :rocket:
